newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real ends off, mkt awaits mini-band drop.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real ends off, mkt awaits mini-band drop.

text.p: Brazil's real dipped 0.01 percent to close at 1.0471 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market on the first day of trade after the four-day Carnival break, dealers said.

Trading was bland in the forex market which opened at midday today, two and a half hours later than usual. Players said they expected a new slide in the real-dollar mini-band between Thursday and Friday.
"The market was still working at a Carnival-like pace. Nobody wanted to do anything," one dealer said.
The current mini-band was set last Thursday at between 1.0470 and 1.0520 reais per dollar.
In late afternoon, the Central Bank bought dollars at 1.0470 reais per U.S. unit to drain excess dollars from the market.
Last Friday, commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts posted a $189.9 million surplus.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real fell 0.04 percent to end at 1.0533 per dollar.
The illegal parallel market remained closed today in the wake of the Carnival holiday, and will reopen on Thursday.
